thread:
nina: FYI our onboarding example started dragging ~600KB of node shims after the latest SDK types change. Edge build failed with `ReferenceError: global is not defined`.

sam: Sounds like types introduced a runtime import (e.g. `import { Readable } from 'stream'`) in index.d.ts — types should never cause consumers to pull node builtins.

nina: yep, index.d.ts references `stream` for a helper type but runtime path in browser never uses it. consumer bundler pulled Buffer/tslib helpers.

yuri: Quick fixes: 1) split node-only types into a separate `types/node.d.ts`; 2) add conditional exports so `import` resolves ESM browser build. Example:
```
"exports": { ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs", "types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts" } }
```

kevin: Also set `sideEffects": false` in package.json (and mark any real side-effect files explicitly). Provide `browser` entry pointing to an ESM browser-targeted build to avoid polyfills.

sam: Another pitfall: re-export wrapper `dist/index.js` that conditionally requires CJS can force bundlers to include node shims. Make sure top-level import path is pure ESM.

nina: I pushed a small PR: split types, add exports, set `sideEffects:false`, and added `dist/esm/browser.mjs`. Example CI action builds an edge app and checks gzipped size.

ci-bot: CI: examples/edge-app size check failed (gzipped 412KB > 200KB). Artifacts: /artifacts/1769023501.

yuri: Remaining ~180KB looks like tslib helpers + small process shim. Option: set `tsconfig.importHelpers=true` and publish `tslib` as a dependency so helpers aren't inlined. Also change any top-level `if (typeof window === 'undefined') require('x')` to dynamic import inside init to avoid static analysis traps.

kevin: Agree. Add an examples/edge-app GH action and a short note in SDK onboarding docs: "Edge compatibility: ESM entry, sideEffects:false, avoid node types in main d.ts".

nina: thanks — will update PR with tslib and tweak CI threshold while we iterate. will ping for reviews. :rocket:
